title: Prove Me Wrong: choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned "Notes to the Accounts", which treats your thesis like a company's audited statements. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Notes to the Accounts
options.lineage: Indian annual reports: audited statements, the auditor's opinion, notes to the accounts
options.thesis: Your thesis is audited the way a company's books are. Each sentence gets an auditor's opinion: Unmodified, Qualified, Adverse or Disclaimer.
materials: this quarter vs last quarter columns
options.viewport: A deep statement-green left rail with stock search, the Nifty 50 list and the Scoreboard link. The main area is the thesis as a three-row statement: sentence | opinion | Note refs | this quarter vs last quarter. A side panel holds the cited notes. A 'Run audit' button and an 'as at' quarter control sit at the top.
options.risk: Can read corporate and dry if the opinion stamps and colour roles are set timidly. The stamp has to be the hero.

raised.raise: Struck-and-restated: an Adverse sentence is struck through and a 'Restated' version appears beneath it, using the restatement idiom of financial statements.
One live axis: the 'as at' quarter control re-runs every opinion continuously, so you watch your thesis age quarter by quarter.
Symmetry: evidence for and against is drawn mirrored around each sentence's centre line, so the balance reads before any words.
Honest resolution: every forecast is shown at the precision the model actually has, as ranges with no false decimals.
A hard budget: three sentences, metered like a tape side, so a thesis can't sprawl.

regions.label: thesis statement: sentence | opinion stamp | notes
signals: return range, volatility, regime, call drift (with track record)

options.label: Third Umpire Review
options.lineage: cricket DRS: ball-tracking, the umpire's call, the big-screen verdict
options.thesis: You challenge your own view the way a player reviews a decision: ball-tracking (the return range) projects the path and the big screen says OUT, NOT OUT or UMPIRE'S CALL.
options.viewport: A navy shell. The thesis sits on the left and each sentence gets a verdict band. The centre is a projected 20-day return path drawn as a cone with the real outcome overlaid. 'Reviews remaining' pips show the live-check quota.
options.risk: Instantly familiar to an Indian audience, which is also why it can tip into a cricket costume and feel gimmicky to a non-cricket recruiter.

options.label: Terminal Yellow
options.thesis: One decision at a time: a saturated yellow band always shows the next thing that would make you wrong, and roughly how far off it is.
options.viewport: A sticky yellow band shows 'Next test: Q3 concall, 18 days', with the thesis rows scrolling beneath it.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and wins on clarity, but retail investors don't recognise the world, so it holds only one of the two axes.
options.risk: A full yellow field gets tiring on a screen you stay on for long, which works against 'easy on the eye'.

options.label: Lexicon Shoulder
options.thesis: Evidence as marginalia in a shoulder column, with colour kept inside plates.
options.viewport: A text column with evidence notes down the outside margin.
options.risk: Lands on the cream-and-serif editorial default.
options.case: Investors don't identify with it, and it reads as a book rather than a tool.

options.label: Variable Specimen
options.thesis: Conviction as font weight, driven live by one axis.
options.viewport: Thesis sentences thinning as evidence undermines them.
options.risk: A typographer's toy that investors wouldn't recognise.
options.kept: One live axis remaps the whole page (the as-at quarter control).

options.label: Dance Score
options.thesis: Evidence for and against as mirrored columns around a centre staff.
options.viewport: A vertical staff with the thesis as the spine.
options.kept: Mirrored for/against symmetry around each sentence.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.kept: Show numbers only at the precision the model really has.

options.label: Mixtape J-card
options.thesis: Bull side A, bear side B.
options.viewport: A folded card with two sides.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean fintech research dashboard (Tickertape or Koyfin level of craft), done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, price chart up top, thesis and signal cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every stock app, which is exactly what you said to avoid.
